questions.problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{(2{n}^{2}+3)(2{n}^{2}-3)}{2n(5{n}^{3}-1)}$ for $n\ge 1?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we multiply out the numerator and denominator of the sequence and get

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(2{n}^{2}+3)(2{n}^{2}-3)}{2n(5{n}^{3}-1)}=\frac{4{n}^{4}-9}{10{n}^{4}-2n}.
$$

So to find the limit, we will need to compute

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{4{n}^{4}-9}{10{n}^{4}-2n}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $10{n}^{4},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{4}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{4{n}^{4}-9}{10{n}^{4}-2n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{4{n}^{4}}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{9}{{n}^{4}})}{(\frac{10{n}^{4}}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{2n}{{n}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(4-\frac{9}{{n}^{4}})}{(10-\frac{2}{{n}^{3}})} \\  & =\frac{4-0}{10-0} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence converges and its limit is $\frac{2}{5}.$

questions.problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{8{n}^{5}-2n}{8{n}^{4}-2}$ for $n\ge 1?$
questions.worked_solution:
The dominant term in the denominator is $8{n}^{4},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{4}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{8{n}^{5}-2n}{8{n}^{4}-2} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{8{n}^{5}}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{2n}{{n}^{4}})}{(\frac{8{n}^{4}}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{2}{{n}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(8n-\frac{2}{{n}^{3}})}{(8-\frac{2}{{n}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{8n-0}{8-0} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }n \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

The limit does not exist, so the sequence diverges.

questions.problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{1-{n}^{4}}{3{n}^{2}+5}$ for $n\ge 1?$
questions.worked_solution:
The dominant term  in the denominator is $3{n}^{2}$, so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{2}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1-{n}^{4}}{3{n}^{2}+5} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{{n}^{2}}-\frac{{n}^{4}}{{n}^{2}})}{(\frac{3{n}^{2}}{{n}^{2}}+\frac{5}{{n}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{{n}^{2}}-{n}^{2})}{(3+\frac{5}{{n}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{0-{n}^{2}}{3+0} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }(-\frac{{n}^{2}}{3}) \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

The limit does not exist, so the sequence diverges.

questions.problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{(3n-2)(3n+2)}{n(1-9n)}$ for $n\ge 1?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we multiply out the numerator and denominator of the sequence and get

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(3n-2)(3n+2)}{n(1-9n)}=\frac{9{n}^{2}-4}{n-9{n}^{2}}.
$$

So to find the limit, we will need to compute

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{9{n}^{2}-4}{n-9{n}^{2}}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $-9{n}^{2},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{2}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{9{n}^{2}-4}{n-9{n}^{2}} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{9{n}^{2}}{{n}^{2}}-\frac{4}{{n}^{2}})}{(\frac{n}{{n}^{2}}-\frac{9{n}^{2}}{{n}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(9-\frac{4}{{n}^{2}})}{(\frac{1}{n}-9)} \\  & =\frac{9-0}{0-9} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence converges and its limit is $-1.$

To determine whether the sequence converges or diverges, we need to determine the limit of the sequence as $n$ approaches infinity:

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{12n+1}{3n}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $3n,$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by $n$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{12n+1}{3n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{12n}{n}+\frac{1}{n})}{\frac{3n}{n}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{12+\frac{1}{n}}{3} \\  & =\frac{12+0}{3} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence converges, and its limit is $4.$
